[HD 137010 b] HD 137010 b is an exoplanet candidate detected by the Kepler's K2 mission of NASA. Orbiting the K-type dwarf star HD 137010 in the constellation of Libra, it is located approximately 146 light-years from the Solar System. The candidate was identified from a single 10-hour transit event observed during K2 Campaign 15 in 2017, suggesting an orbital period of about 355 days, nearly identical to that of Earth. With a radius of 1.06 times that of Earth, it is classified as a potential Super-Earth or Earth analog, likely rocky in composition. Due to its host star's lower luminosity, HD 137010 b receives only about 29% of the incident flux that Earth does, placing it near the outer edge of the system's habitable zone with an estimated equilibrium temperature around −68 °C (−90 °F), potentially colder than Mars. Confirmation as a genuine exoplanet requires additional transits or alternative observations, which may be pursued with missions like TESS or CHEOPS. | other articles: HD 137010, HD 139139
